einstellungen.text: Next to you sits a boy who only exists in the window.
On the bus, the seat is empty. Just a dark, wet spot on the cushion. You don't turn your head an inch.
In the window, he sits completely still. Maybe twelve. His schoolbag is dripping.
He doesn't look evil. He looks like he's been waiting a very long time.
He's holding something. Very slowly, he turns it toward the glass.
An old bus ticket. November eighth, nineteen ninety-eight. Millbrook Lane, twelve twelve.
The box for the stamp is empty. Nobody ever stamped this ticket.
Up front, Henrik looks in the rearview mirror. He sees the boy too.
His hands are shaking on the wheel.
Henrik knows his name. He's known it for twenty-eight years.
Paul doesn't look at Henrik. And he doesn't look at you.
He's staring at one spot. The red button on the pole.
You don't understand what he wants. Not yet.
Then it turns ice cold beside you. The air smells like lake weed.
The cushion next to you slowly sinks in. Paul is sitting on the real bus now.
